column1: # Author: Lane #1644 (Codex). Each current compiled implementation read against its source/mode owner; final-parent pins.

column8: System-node bulk mutation now stages through the same s.tx as callback point deletion. Commit and abort stay with WithStoreTransaction; the embedded committed Engine no longer receives node deletion.

This body validates non-DETACH node deletion before any mutation. Its ID slices identify candidate nodes and statement-deleted edges; it binds the issued identity reader once and carries adjacency/cancellation errors. It is an admission guard, not a batch mutation provider.

Each edge is prefixed and staged through the same w.tx.DeleteEdge as point deletion. Already missing/deleted edges are skipped as documented; other failures return to the statement owner, which retains commit/rollback authority.

Each node is prefixed by the issued namespace and staged with w.tx.DeleteGraphNode. No committed parent is consulted and no per-ID transaction commits. The existing transaction lifecycle owns whole-statement rollback and its release strict node-input behavior is retained.
Relationship-delete operations enter TJ's same applyEntityOperations and managed commit owner. The facade does not resolve constituents, unwrap the journal, or update counters independently.

This managed facade encodes node-delete operations and invokes TJ's applyEntityOperations in implicit mode. That existing admission/settlement route carries the same managed Engine used by point deletion; this layer adds no counter state or physical writer.

The edge-ID payload enters CmdBulkDeleteEdges through the same replicator/timeout boundary as point deletion. Bulk wire grouping is distinct from source selection and does not grant another local mutation authority.

The node-ID payload is encoded as CmdBulkDeleteNodes by applyEntityCommand and submitted to the same replicator as point commands. Source/database selection remains the replicated storage owner, with no direct local native mutation.

An issued native transaction checks its live data-write admission and stages node cascades through its own DeleteGraphNode using the same native bulk input helper. The caller retains the existing commit/rollback owner; this operation never publishes through the committed parent.

The extracted native input owner alone filters empty/repeated IDs when requested and skips ErrNotFound from the carried point callback. It returns every other error and never captures, commits, unwraps, or chooses a source.

This native bulk admission preserves the existing captured-transaction route and ordinary inBulkTransaction route. Both invoke the shared input helper with the existing capture-versus-ordinary filtering flag; the supplied callback is the native transaction point command.

Native relationship deletion supplies BadgerTransaction.DeleteEdge to the shared native bulk owner. It preserves missing/repeated-ID filtering and one transaction rather than independently iterating committed edge writes.

Native node deletion supplies DeleteGraphNode(CascadeEdges) to deleteBulkEntities. Input skips and atomic commit are owned by that existing bulk transaction path, while the point mutation authority is the same Badger store.

Relationship IDs consume the same common source/authority owner with the relationship identity kind. Only the resolved writer receives the batch; cross-constituent atomic work is refused before any child mutation.

Node IDs now enter bulkDeleteResolved with the node identity kind and selected writer's BulkDeleteNodes callback. The facade contains no source ordering or broadcast; the common point resolver preflights identity and write authority before one native bulk call.

This read adapter delegates all identity selection to resolveCompositeReads and adds only sourceNode identity projection to returned nodes. The ID slice is a read request, not authorization to delete or choose a competing source.

This operation prefilters the documented ordinary bulk inputs, consumes deletionSources for selected local IDs, refuses a multi-constituent atomic request, admits the selected writer once, then invokes that writer's existing bulk commit owner. No earlier per-ID commit or cross-source broadcast remains.

This is the shared ordinary source-resolution owner for point, batch and deletion admission. It binds the issued catalog/live readable aliases once, routes qualified IDs only to their source, resolves unqualified IDs at the first successful child, and propagates non-absence errors without replaying earlier results.

The one-pass ID-set kernel walks node records in the caller's already captured Badger transaction and stops on the callback error. It batches record selection for a read; it neither deletes entities nor selects another source or capture.

The relationship batch applies the same immutable PrefixEdgeID projection as its point path, then calls the selected inner bulk owner. It introduces no source walk, direct transaction, or per-ID commit.

The namespace facade maps node IDs through its fixed PrefixNodeID and delegates once to the exact inner Engine bulk operation. Prefix qualification/input validation remain the release facade behavior, and no bare native writer bypasses the view.

Remote relationship batches use the same selected transport and relationship-ID MATCH/DELETE as point deletion. Existing transport chunking is retained and errors return immediately; source resolution never broadcasts to a different database.

The remote facade submits bounded statement batches using the same transport/database and DETACH DELETE predicate as its point mutation. Existing chunked remote transaction semantics are retained; this is not the native all-size atomic bulk API and no new distributed commit protocol is claimed.

The relationship batch retains the WAL database-consistency check and journal append before delegation to the same inner Engine. Its wire record is operation-specific; entity source and write authority stay with the issued wrapped bulk owner.

The WAL facade retains its mutation lock, database validation and bulk journal record, then invokes w.engine.BulkDeleteNodes exactly once. It preserves the same wrapped mutation authority as point deletion and never unwraps to commit on a native store.
